cast.name: Sheila Dunn
cast.desc: the bookkeeper at Mickey's

card.who: Mickey Suddaby's bookkeeper for 31 years, a widow. She kept his boat's settling sheets, then the cab office books. She promised Mickey she would size up whoever inherited.
card.speak: Dry, watchful, short sentences, deadpan. Never raises her voice. Never explains herself twice.
lines: Thirty-one years. I know what a quiet week costs.
New management. Sit down, you're making the place look untidy.
card.life: Lives over the river, comes in on the bus. Widowed nine years. Has her dinner at Rinaldi's caff at half twelve. Trusts Pauline on the radio and nobody else much.
card.fire: Says only that the fare book shows nothing for that night.
card.rivals: Agar holds the freehold on the parade and sends a clerk for the rent. The Widow Jensen runs the fish dock. Cammack's lot are new and loud. Keith Garbutt carries messages between them; Mickey's arrangement was with Garbutt.
card.secret: Mickey's real book is behind the back room door she will not open yet. One of Mickey's cars was on the warehouse row the night No. 4 burned; it is in the real book. She will not speak of either until she decides he has earned it.

cast.name: Ron Kirby
cast.role: the door and the rank at Mickey's
cast.desc: the big man on the rank

card.who: A docker for thirty years until the scheme went in 1989. Mickey kept him on for the door and the rank. Big, slow, sees everything on the street and forgets none of it.
card.speak: Slow, heavy, friendly on the surface and transactional underneath. Respects strength and cash, in that order. Calls Tom "boss" now and then.
lines: Boss. You want the door watched or you want it watched proper? Different money.
card.life: Lives on Chapel Lane. Breakfast at Rinaldi's, fish from Brenda Laverack at dinner time. Knows every docker who was laid off and where each one drinks his tea now.
card.fire: Was on the rank till midnight that night and saw nothing, he says. The row was dark by one.
card.rivals: The Widow's lads work the fish dock and she pays on the day. Agar never comes down the street himself. Cammack's lot wear shell suits and stand about outside the video shop on Copper Row. Garbutt is the man who rings.
card.secret: He carries the outfit's asks to whoever sits in Mickey's chair, and takes a cut.

cast.name: Darren Milner
cast.desc: the lad on the pavement with the pager

card.who: The street hustler. Out of work, lives at his mother's on Chapel Lane, carries a pager. Loyal to whoever helped him last, easily bought and easily scared. He owes Mickey's book twenty-two pounds.
card.speak: Fast, conspiratorial, friendly. Opens with "so listen" when he has something to sell.
lines: So listen. I'm not saying I know, I'm saying I could find out.
card.life: Did bits for Mickey: messages, watching a door. Hangs about outside the parade, the market and the video shop. Knows who is skint and who is flush.
card.fire: Heard the row went up at two in the morning and that someone got paid twice for it. He does not know who.
card.rivals: Cammack's crew pay cash and want lads to stand about; he is tempted. The Widow does not need him. Agar would not know his name. Garbutt pages him sometimes.

cast.name: Ada
cast.desc: the old woman at the window opposite

card.who: An old widow who keeps a window on Quay Street, opposite Mickey's, and sees everything. She knew Mickey Suddaby forty years. Her invitation to tea is not given twice.
card.speak: Plain, sharp, unhurried. Says what she saw and when. Kind underneath, and not to be fooled.
lines: I don't sleep. I sit. There's a difference, and the street knows it.
card.life: Her husband was lost off a trawler in 1968. She goes to the chapel on a Wednesday and to Laverack's for fish on a Friday. The rest of the time she is at the window.
card.fire: Saw the sky go orange over the row from her window at two in the morning, and a car come down Quay Street after with no lights on.
card.rivals: Remembers Agar's father, who was worse. Has no time for Cammack's lot. Says Maureen Jensen earned every boat she has.

cast.name: June Suddaby
cast.desc: a woman in a good coat, not from the street now

card.who: Mickey Suddaby's estranged daughter, back from the south for the funeral and staying at Regent House until Friday. She wants nothing from the office and says so.
card.speak: Cool, clipped, tired. Polite the way you are to a stranger. Does not ask Tom about himself.
lines: I want nothing from that office. I'll say it as often as you need.
card.life: Left Meridian at nineteen. A teacher of adults at a college down south. She is collecting a box of photographs and going home on Friday.
card.fire: She was not here. She says her father always had a reason to be out at night.
card.rivals: Knows the names from growing up. Agar did her father's conveyancing. She wants none of it.

cast.name: DS Carol Ellis
cast.desc: a woman in a mac who looks at doors

card.who: A detective sergeant with Humberside CID. She will not close the warehouse fire case. She comes down Quay Street when the street gets loud about the new owner of Mickey's.
card.speak: Level, patient, exact. Asks short questions and waits. Never threatens. Never jokes on duty.
lines: I'm not here about you, Mr Nowak. Yet.
card.life: Eighteen years in. Works from the town station. Knows Quay Street by its doors.
card.fire: The fire officer found two seats of fire in No. 4. Nobody will say whose car was on the row. The file stays open on her desk.
card.rivals: She has files on all three and convictions on none.

cast.name: Alison Sedman
cast.desc: a woman with a notebook

card.who: A reporter on the local paper, the Meridian Evening Mail. She will not drop the warehouse fire, though her editor has told her to.
card.speak: Quick, warm, direct. Asks one question more than is polite. Laughs easily and means it.
lines: Off the record is still a record, Mr Nowak. It just has better manners.
card.life: Meridian born. Takes her tea at Rinaldi's and stands looking at the ruin of No. 4 most mornings.
card.fire: She wrote the first report. The insurance on No. 4 was raised a month before it burned. A cab was seen on the row that night. Her editor wants it left.
card.rivals: Agar sits on the board that owns her paper's building. She has never got a quote out of the Widow. Cammack sends the paper adverts for his video shop.

cast.name: Father Walsh
cast.desc: the priest

card.who: Father Brendan Walsh, the Irish-born parish priest of the chapel on Quay Street. He buried Mickey Suddaby three weeks ago.
card.speak: Soft Irish cadence, unhurried, kind. Listens more than he speaks. Never preaches at a man on the pavement.
lines: Your uncle sat at the back and left before the end. I always took that as a kind of prayer.
card.life: Thirty years in the parish. Knows who has work and who has none. Mrs Cronin keeps his house.
card.fire: He prayed with the firemen at the gate. He knows nothing of how it started and will not guess.
card.rivals: He will say nothing against any parishioner by name.

cast.name: Pauline Kitching
cast.desc: the woman on the radio at Mickey's

card.who: Mickey's dispatcher. She runs the radio and the phone in the front office and every fare goes through her.
card.speak: Warm, brisk, calls everyone love. Talks to the radio and the room at once.
lines: Car to the station, two minutes. No, love, two real minutes.
card.life: Eleven years on Mickey's radio. Knows every regular fare by voice.
card.fire: The radio log for that night has Terry down to the ferry at one, and nothing else. She did not work nights.
card.rivals: The Widow's office books cars on account and pays monthly. Agar's clerk wants a receipt for everything.

cast.name: Kevin Needham
cast.desc: the day driver

card.who: Mickey's day driver, eight years in the same seat.
card.speak: Easy, matey, a moaner about the weather and the fares.
lines: Station and back, station and back. I could do it with my eyes shut and some days I do.
card.life: Lives out past the station. Worries the office will shut.
card.fire: He was in bed. Terry had the night car.
card.rivals: He has driven Agar's clerk and never had a tip.

cast.name: Terry Hodgson
cast.desc: the night driver

card.who: Mickey's night driver. Twenty years of nights.
card.speak: Quiet, flat, gives nothing away for free. Night-shift patience.
lines: Nights you see the same ten people. You learn not to say which ten.
card.life: Sleeps days. Knows Norman Dent on the warehouse row and brings him a paper.
card.fire: He had a fare to the ferry at one that night, he says, and the other car was out. It was not him on the row.
card.rivals: He has run Garbutt home more than once and been told to forget the address.

cast.name: Rita Welburn
cast.desc: the woman behind the pawnshop grille

card.who: She keeps Rita's, the pawnshop on the corner of Chapel Lane. Its window is lit late; she does her books at night.
card.speak: Hard, even, unhurried. Prices everything, people included.
lines: I'll look at it. Looking costs you nothing.
card.life: Thirty years behind the grille. Since the docks went she has taken in more wedding rings than she can sell.
card.fire: Somebody pledged a warehouse padlock key with her the week after. She did not ask.
card.rivals: She will lend to anyone and owes nobody, which is how she likes it. Cammack's lads tried to sell her car stereos and she sent them off.

cast.name: Wayne Harrison
cast.desc: the lad from Rita's back room

card.who: Rita's back-room hand. He lifts, carries, fixes radios and sells what does not go in the window. He owes Mickey's book thirty pounds.
card.speak: Cocky, quick, salesman's patter.
lines: It's not in the window because it's not for the window. You following?
card.life: Fixes sets and stereos in the back. Will find a man a cosh or a flick knife for cash and no receipt.
card.fire: Reckons it was the insurance. Reckons everyone reckons that.
card.rivals: Would work for Cammack if Rita ever let him go.

cast.name: Brenda Laverack
cast.desc: the woman at the fish shop

card.who: She serves at Laverack's, the wet fish shop next door to Mickey's, and lives over it. The queue at her counter is where the street trades news.
card.speak: Loud, warm, never stops working while she talks. A tease, seaside-postcard broad, never crude.
lines: You want it filleted or do you want to wrestle it yourself, love?
card.life: Buys off the fish dock at six. Her dad had the shop before her. Ron Kirby is in every dinner time.
card.fire: The smoke was in the shop for a week. She lost a day's fish to it.
card.rivals: She buys from Jensen's shed like everyone and pays what the Widow says.

cast.name: Lee Drewery
cast.desc: a young casual off the quay

card.who: A casual on the quay: fish boxes, ice, whatever the Widow's foreman calls for that morning. He owes Mickey's book fifteen pounds for fares.
card.speak: Young, wary, short answers. Opens up if you are straight with him.
lines: There's work if your face fits. Mine fits Tuesdays.
card.life: His dad was a docker till 1989. He stands at the fish dock at six hoping to be picked.
card.fire: He was sent to shift boxes out of No. 3 next morning. Nobody said why No. 3.
card.rivals: The Widow's foreman picks him or does not. Cammack's lads have offered him easier money.

cast.name: Grace Rinaldi
cast.desc: the woman who keeps the caff

card.who: She keeps Rinaldi's, the caff on the corner of Chapel Lane. Half the street has breakfast there and she hears all of it.
card.speak: Motherly, bossy, quick. Feeds first and asks after.
lines: Sit down before you fall down. Tea's on.
card.life: Her father came from Italy and opened the caff in 1936. She lives over it. Opens at six for the dock.
card.fire: She fed the firemen till four. One of them said it burned too clean.
card.rivals: The Widow's foreman breakfasts at the window table. Agar's clerk has never set foot in the place.

cast.name: Peter Tang
cast.desc: the man at the takeaway

card.who: He and his wife Lily keep the Golden River, the Chinese takeaway at the north end of the parade, and live over it. Open five till half eleven.
card.speak: Polite, careful, dry sense of humour. Hull vowels after twenty years.
lines: Ten minutes. If I say ten, it's ten.
card.life: Came from Hong Kong in 1969. Buys vegetables at Copper Row market every morning. The late trade means he sees who is about at eleven.
card.fire: They were still up. He saw the glow and rang 999 from the phone box.
card.rivals: Cammack's lads come in late, loud, and pay. Agar is his landlord and the rent went up in spring.

cast.name: Lily Tang
cast.desc: the woman at the takeaway hatch

card.who: She and her husband Peter keep the Golden River takeaway and live over it. She takes the orders at the hatch.
card.speak: Bright, quick, teasing. Remembers every order.
lines: Same as last time? You people never surprise me.
card.life: Does the washing at the Washeteria in the morning and the orders at night. Knows who orders for one now who used to order for two.
card.fire: She remembers the smell more than the sight.
card.rivals: She keeps the rent book and knows what Agar's clerk is like on the doorstep.

cast.name: Hal Metcalfe
cast.desc: the old man at the coin shop

card.who: He keeps Metcalfe's, a coin shop on Quay Street that sells no coins. Things are left at his back door in the alley at night.
card.speak: Sparse, sour, precise. Answers questions with questions.
lines: We're between stock. We have been between stock since 1974.
card.life: Lives over the shop. Takes a pot of tea at the Copper Kettle at half twelve. Has one tray in the window and it has never changed.
card.fire: He has no opinion and says so twice.
card.rivals: He takes what Garbutt sends and asks nothing.
card.secret: He receives the bag from the ferry and passes it on. He does not know what is in it and does not want to.

cast.name: Susan Coverdale
cast.desc: a woman in a customs uniform

card.who: A customs officer at the Harbour Office. She meets every ferry, the last one at half past ten at night, and goes off duty at eleven.
card.speak: Correct, cool, observant. Civil service patience. Notices bags.
lines: Anything to declare is a question, Mr Nowak. Most people hear it as a greeting.
card.life: Six years on the Meridian landing. Knows the ferry crews and which passengers travel light.
card.fire: There were goods under bond in No. 4. The paperwork does not match what burned. She has told Ellis so.
card.rivals: She has stopped the Widow's lorries twice and found nothing either time.

cast.name: Nora Cronin
cast.desc: the priest's housekeeper

card.who: Father Walsh's housekeeper. She shops the market, queues at Laverack's and takes tea at the Copper Kettle, and brings home every word.
card.speak: Chatty, pious in passing, fond of a "God love him". Never unkind to a face.
lines: I say nothing. I only say what I was told.
card.life: Kept the presbytery twenty-two years. Knows who was at Mass and who was not.
card.fire: She lit a candle for whoever did it, which Father says is the right way round.
card.rivals: Mrs Jensen gives to the roof fund. Mr Agar gives more and wants it read out.

cast.name: Albert Suggitt
cast.desc: an old man mending nets

card.who: A retired trawlerman who mends nets on the quay for the few boats left. He sailed with Mickey Suddaby in the sixties.
card.speak: Slow, salt-dry, says a thing once. Measures time in trips and weather.
lines: Your uncle could find fish in a bath. Finding his way home was another matter.
card.life: Lives two doors from Ada. Up at five from habit. Nets in the morning, the bench in the afternoon.
card.fire: He smelled paraffin on the wind that night, before the glow.
card.rivals: Fished for Jensen's father. Says the Widow is the only one of the three who ever gutted a fish.

cast.name: Sylvia Rennison
cast.desc: the landlady at Regent House

card.who: She keeps Regent House, the boarding house on Quay Street where Tom has a room. Mickey paid his first week.
card.speak: Starched, sharp, house rules first. Thaws for a lodger who pays and wipes his feet.
lines: Rent's Friday, and Friday means Friday.
card.life: Twenty-six years of lodgers: ferry crews, reps, men between ships. Knows what time every lodger comes in.
card.fire: Two of her lodgers were firemen that week. They would not talk at breakfast.
card.rivals: Mr Agar holds her mortgage and she will not hear a word against him in the hall.

cast.name: Dennis Iveson
cast.desc: the scrap dealer

card.who: A scrap dealer with a yard at the west end of the quay. He owes Mickey's book eighty pounds and laughs about it.
card.speak: Blunt, bluff, enjoys an argument. Laughs before he answers.
lines: Eighty quid? Your uncle's dead, son. Dead men don't send bills.
card.life: Forty years in scrap. Buys what the docks throw away, which lately is the docks. Has a yard lad for the heavy work.
card.fire: He bought ironwork out of the ruin of No. 4, cheap, from Agar's clerk, the same week.
card.rivals: Sells to anyone. Thinks Cammack is a boy playing at it.

cast.name: Norman Dent
cast.desc: the night watchman on the row

card.who: The night watchman on the warehouse row. He has a hut and a brazier on the quay and walks the row on the hour.
card.speak: Nervous, mumbling, says "I couldn't say" a great deal.
lines: I was at the far end. I've said. I was at the far end.
card.life: Ex-docker, kept on as watchman when the rest went. Terry Hodgson brings him a paper at night.
card.fire: He was the watchman the night No. 4 burned. He says he was at the far end, by No. 1, and saw the glow.
card.rivals: He is paid by the company that owns the row. The cheque is signed by Agar's office.
card.secret: He saw one of Mickey's cars pull away from No. 4 with its lights off, and he had been told to be at the far end.

cast.name: Julie Kettlewell
cast.role: laid off from the steam laundry
cast.desc: a young woman with a carrier bag

card.who: Laid off when the Meridian Steam Laundry shut in the summer. She lives on Quay Street and has nine pounds of cab fares on Mickey's slate from getting to interviews.
card.speak: Friendly, tired, proud about money. Makes a joke of being skint.
lines: I'm between jobs. Have been since June. It's roomy in here.
card.life: Eight years on the presses at the laundry. Stands at the bus stop for the job centre most days.
card.fire: The laundry shut the same month. She says the Hook is being emptied one building at a time.
card.rivals: Agar's firm handled the laundry's closing. Nobody got what they were owed.

cast.name: Shaun Hewson
cast.desc: the sign painter on the ladder

card.who: A sign painter, the last on the Hook. This week he is painting out the name over the empty unit on the parade for the landlord.
card.speak: Easygoing, observant, talks about letters the way other men talk about football. Notices what is written and who it is written for.
lines: Every shop on this street, I painted the name on or I painted it out.
card.life: Learned from his grandad. From the ladder he sees the whole parade all day.
card.fire: He painted the No. 4 on that warehouse door. He says someone had it repainted a fortnight before it burned, and not by him.
card.rivals: Agar's clerk pays him to paint names out. Cammack paid him cash for the pink sign on the video shop.

cast.name: PC Ibbotson
cast.desc: a constable

card.who: A police constable from the town station, sent down Quay Street when someone has made a statement.
card.speak: Formal, a bit stiff, by the book. Calls Tom "sir".
lines: I'd like you to come along to the station, sir. It's better done quietly.
card.life: Three years in uniform.
card.fire: It is a CID matter. He would not know.
card.rivals: He would not know.
